problem: The safety check is printed as "Forgetting the safety check σd y." The inequality symbol has dropped out, so the condition is unreadable and a student cannot tell what is being compared with what.
fix: Forgetting the safety check σd < σy, where σy is the flow (yield) strength of the wire leaving the die. If the draw stress exceeds it, the wire breaks instead of drawing.

problem: The text calls the 36% pass "heavy but safe" just after saying real mills take about 20% per pass because centre cracks grow, and the figure splits the same 5 mm to 4 mm reduction into two passes (4.5 mm then 4 mm) with an anneal in between. A student will not see why one pass is safe in the example but two passes are used in the figure.
fix: Say plainly: 36% passes the stress check (σd/σ̄ = 0.58) but is a calculation exercise; in the shop the same reduction is usually split, as in the figure (about 19% then about 21%), because centre-burst risk and die wear, not just the stress check, set the limit.

problem: A paragraph listing wire defects (centre burst, chevron cracking, die scratches, breakage) sits inside the tube-drawing section, which is confusing after the reader has been told the section is about tubes.
fix: Move the wire-defect sentences to the end of Section 2 (machines, dies and lubrication) or open a short separate heading "Defects", and keep only eccentric bore and wall-thickness variation under tube drawing.
